newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel urges opening insurance mart to banks.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel urges opening insurance mart to banks.

text.p: The Insurance Council, an advisory panel to Japan's finance minister, proposed after protracted debate that banks be allowed to enter the insurance market through subsidiaries, a Finance Ministry official said on Friday.

In a final proposal on steps to implement Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms to liberalise the nation's financial markets, the council on Friday recommended the entry of banks and brokers into the insurance sector through subsidiaries by the end of 2001.

"The council proposed that other types of financial institutions be allowed to participate in the insurance markets without any restriction in the range of business," a Finance Ministry official said.
The council approved the proposal after four-and-a-half months of contentious discussions, and it follows a sweeping reform of the insurance industry last year, he said.

Allowing banks to enter the insurance sector was one of the most difficult issues to resolve, as life insurance companies feared that they would lose business to financially strong banks, industry sources said.

The insurance industry agreed to a compromise under which banks would not be allowed to sell insurance policies through their vast branch networks, but would instead have to do business through subsidiaries, they said.

Another MOF official said that the Financial System Research Council proposed allowing commercial banks to issue corporate bonds as a method of raising long-term funds, but did not recommend that the banks be allowed to issue bank debentures.

The Council, which is concerned primarily with Japan's banking policies, is also one of the advisory panels which Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto asked to help set details of his "Big Bang" plans to liberalise the nation's financial markets by 2001.
Under current laws, long-term credit banks are allowed to issue bank debentures as a major means of raising funds, although commercial banks are not allowed to issue such debentures.
Members of the panel expect the deregulation of bond issues by commercial banks to help the banks diversify their methods of raising long-term funds.
